title: Pass model from server to JS client to support arbitrary realtime models
description:
The client-side JS hardcoded model="gpt-realtime" on the WebRTC SDP call, ignoring the model arg passed to realtime_server. This made it impossible to use newer models like gpt-realtime-2.

Server (R and Python) now returns a JSON payload {value, model}; the JS openConnection parses it (falling back to bare string for compat) and uses the model in the /realtime/calls?model=... request.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This PR morphed a bit into a general bug squashing update. I first fixed the tool output to realtime then fixed the cascading things that it led to. Will keep this open as I make necessary updates.

title: Add plot interaction functionality with click/brush support
description:
This is very rough, but it's a start. Allows you to tell the model you want to feed it coordinates using clicks, or coordinate ranges using brushes.

* "Add text annotations to just the points I click."
* "Zoom in by setting the x and y limits to a range that I brush."
* "Remove the outlier data that I select by using a brush."

When a user request is issued to the model that it thinks needs clicking/brushing, the model tells the app to switch the plot output to that interaction mode.

When a click or brush event occurs, a text message is sent to the model in the form of "The user clicked on the plot at data coordinates (_x_, _y_).)" or "The user brushed a region on the plot from data coordinates (_x1_, _y1_) to (_x2_, _y2_).)" Then the model is immediately instructed to begin a new response.

There's something pretty broken right now if you try to talk and click at the same time. I think it forces the model to "multitask" in a way it definitely cannot. I'm not sure how to fix it but I suspect we'll need to closely monitor the events being returned from the API to keep track of what state we're in (is the user talking? is the model already generating a response?) and maybe hold off on sending the click until just the right moment.
